entry-web.description: Where the browser starts: the router, the document with its Splash for iOS, the offline page, and one thin route for each Place. The router reaches the routes through the generated route tree, so nothing imports them

entry-worker.description: Where the Worker starts: /rpc goes to the Remote Backend, everything else to the app

entry-infra.description: Deployable resources, composed by alchemy.run.ts: the D1 database, the ledger table on it, and the Worker

client-screens.description: What the user sees: the shell around every Place, each Place, the sheets over them, and the parts they share

client-commands.description: The vocabulary: every Command with its keys, the gesture that gives it on a touch screen, the guide to every gesture, and how each sounds and shows when given

client-kit.description: What Ledger needed that no package has yet: sounds made on demand, the Thumb Picker, and what the device can be driven by. Each knows nothing of Ledger

client-gate.description: Where the client starts: reads the Backend Settings chose, runs the app machine on that Backend's services, and runs it again on the other Backend when the User changes it, in memory

client-backends.description: Each Backend's client half, one Layer of the services the app machine needs: who is signed in, how a Session reaches the Backend, and where its copy lives

client-state.description: How the client keeps what its domain promises: a Session over the connection and copy it is given, this device's Settings in IndexedDB, and the copies of every signed-in User

app-state.description: A Session keeps one User's copy; the device's Settings and the copies stand alone

client-domain.description: What the client means, with no I/O: the device's Settings and their table, what an Active Session offers, and the app machine that opens it, over services each Backend provides

server-remote.description: The Remote Backend's server half: the Backend on D1, checked by the Auth Worker, answering /rpc over HTTP

server-local.description: The Local Backend's server half: the Backend on IndexedDB, trusting Local Tokens, as an in-process connection. The only server module the client reaches

server-domain.description: The Backend wherever it runs: the ledger table, the Ledger API's handlers, and the one Layer that checks each call's User. It needs a table adapter and a Resolver, and nothing of any host

shared.description: The words of money, Accounts, Categories, Entries and the currency, with the sums over them and the Ledger API both sides speak

kstack.description: Read top-down: entry starts the browser and the Worker; the client's screens over the Gate, which runs one Backend's services over the client's state and domain; each Backend's server half over the Backend's domain; what both sides speak at the bottom. The client reaches the server only through the Local Backend
